status: Future System panel concepts; illustrative runtime data, no implementation

prompts.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one high-fidelity product screenshot concept for the future LAZERS "System" native OpenCode Desktop side panel. Portrait composition, approximately 1100 by 1450. Only the panel contents: no app sidebar, chat, OS chrome, device frame, marketing headings, perspective or annotations. This is a calm professional developer workbench inspired by Linear's restraint and the causal live activity idea of Agent Radar, NOT a crowded monitoring dashboard. One continuous charcoal neutral surface, native-looking compact UI typography, near-white main text, muted gray supporting type, subtle dividers, 20–24px equivalent side insets. Sparing violet for running, amber for an unresolved decision, desaturated green only for completed work. No neon, glow, gradients, KPI tiles, giant cards, avatars, graphs of token usage, orbiting dots or decorative radar rings.
Header: "System" small bold at left with a tiny live dot; compact "Session" with chevron and an expand icon at right. Underneath a subtle small caption "Retry-safe submission". A small quiet view switch "Flow   Timeline", Flow selected.
Main composition is a very sparse, legible causal execution flow, top to bottom, consuming about upper 60% of the panel. Thin orthogonal dependency lines; a small number of flat compact task nodes, no crossing wires. Two branches clearly convey parallel work. Root node "Persist submission identity" with small check and secondary "Accepted". From it a clean branch splits left to "Document retry contract" with small running arc and secondary "Running", and right to "Test restart recovery" with tiny amber attention mark and secondary "Verification failed". From failed test a downward dependency line leads to a dim flat node "Verify native tool replay", secondary "Waiting on restart recovery". The currently selected failed test has only a very subtle amber outline. On a short lateral line from the failed test show a compact "Architect" node with secondary "Decision needed". Keep the runtime dependency lines visually primary and the decision branch clearly separate. No implication that Architect schedules state transitions. Do not add more nodes, numeric IDs, metrics, mini dashboards or controls.
A thin divider separates a focused lower inspector, exact hierarchy:
small muted "Test restart recovery"
heading "Verification needs a decision"
small readable explanation "A fresh process returned a new task ID."
Then a modest subheading "Delivery"
a small check followed by "Failure saved"
a small check followed by "Architect notified"
a small amber outline dot followed by "Awaiting repair decision"
These three lines show durable outcome delivery, not a log dump.
Then one collapsed disclosure row "Attempt details" and one collapsed disclosure row "Activity". No controls to mark accepted or force ready. Small quiet footer "Concept · example runtime data".
Clear beautiful alignment, generous negative space, immediate understanding of work and why it is waiting. Labels must be readable, exact, and neatly fit nodes. The visual family must match a quiet focused Linear-like tasks panel; the graph exists only because this view explains scheduler causality.

Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one high-fidelity product screenshot concept of the future LAZERS "System" live schedule overview in an expanded native OpenCode Desktop panel, landscape approximately 1600 by 1050. Only panel contents, no surrounding app, sidebar, chat, browser, OS chrome, perspective, marketing or design-board annotations. Minimal Linear-inspired professional developer UI, one flat charcoal neutral background, near-white typography, muted gray secondary type, hairline separators, careful 24px insets. Use restrained violet for running bars, desaturated green completed work, amber verification failure and decisions. No gradients, neon, glowing network, decorative radar rings, dense KPI dashboard, metric cards, avatars or excessive pills.
Header left "System" and small live dot, right quiet "Session" chevron and collapse icon. Below small title "Retry-safe submission"; compact view switch "Flow   Timeline", Timeline selected. Right side of this same row quiet "Last 5 minutes" and "Follow live".
Main area is a simple time-aligned execution timeline, about 65% width on left; quiet selected-item inspector separated by a single vertical hairline on right. No card grid. Timeline has a narrow task-label column, shared time axis "0:00", "1:00", "2:00", "3:00", "4:00", and a slim vertical line labeled "Now" at 4:20. Actual observed history only; no invented completion forecast, no percentage progress. Four rows only:
"Persist submission identity": a short muted completed bar from 0:00 to 1:40 with tiny check.
"Document retry contract": restrained violet running bar from 0:10 to Now, with a very small running glyph at live end.
"Test restart recovery": execution bar from 1:40 to 3:00 followed by a subtle verification segment until 3:50 ending in a tiny amber failure marker. This row selected with a barely tinted background.
"Verify native tool replay": no execution bar, a quiet chain icon with text "Waiting on restart recovery".
Use a few fine orthogonal dependency connectors to show persist precedes restart test and restart test gates replay. The overlapping documentation and restart bars make parallel work instantly clear. Do not connect unrelated rows or fill the timeline with log events.
Beneath those rows, one quieter lane labeled "Architect", with a single amber decision marker at 3:50 and text "Repair decision pending"; no continuously running supervisor bar.
The right inspector has:
small muted "Test restart recovery"
clear heading "Verification failed"
body "A fresh process returned a new task ID."
muted subheading "Next"
"Architect chooses repair or replan."
Then three compact lines with small check icons "Outcome persisted", "Notification delivered", and amber dot "Decision pending".
Collapsed "Attempt details" and "Activity" at bottom. No fake financial numbers, token telemetry, global scope, buttons to accept or force transitions.
Lower-left small muted legend "Execution   Verification   Waiting" with tiny understated marks, and a bottom footer "Concept · example runtime data".
Keep the layout calm, focused, legible and visually coherent with a Linear-like task side panel. This is a scheduler observation tool, not a task management board.
